title: Converting the 4-Round AES Integral Distinguisher
summary: The integral-to-zero-correlation implication holds only for balanced vectorial Boolean functions, while constructing such a hull for four-round AES with extra MixColumns remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For the 4-round AES integral distinguisher with an extra MixColumns operation, determine whether it can be converted into a zero-correlation linear hull and, if so, characterize the conditions under which this conversion is valid; otherwise, characterize why the conversion fails for general integral properties. The implication that an integral property unconditionally yields a zero-correlation linear hull is valid only when the integral property is defined as a balanced vectorial Boolean function, and does not hold in the general case. Constructing such a hull from this AES distinguisher is unresolved.

scope.domain: Symmetric-key cryptanalysis linking AES integral distinguishers and zero-correlation linear hulls.
assumptions: For the known unconditional implication, the integral property is defined as a balanced vectorial Boolean function.
parameters: 4 rounds — the round count of the target AES integral distinguisher
Extra MixColumns operation — the additional operation in the target distinguisher
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the specified AES integral distinguisher can yield a zero-correlation linear hull and characterize either the conditions enabling the conversion or why it fails for general integral properties.

citations.label: Links Among Impossible Differential, Integral and Zero Correlation Linear Cryptanalysis

progress.summary: The source restricts the unconditional integral-to-zero-correlation implication to balanced vectorial Boolean functions and states that it fails for general integral properties. It presents the four-round AES distinguisher with extra MixColumns as a case from which no zero-correlation linear hull had been constructed.
citation_labels: Bing Sun et al., Links Among Impossible Differential, Integral and Zero Correlation Linear Cryptanalysis
